one_liner: Cryptocurrency exchange offering trading, market data, and wallet APIs.

evidence.claim: API keys are self-serve, created from the account's API Management page
evidence.quote: Secure endpoints require a valid API key to be specified and authenticated. API keys can be created on the API Management page of your Binance account.

evidence.claim: Signed endpoints support HMAC, RSA, and Ed25519 API key types
evidence.quote: We support HMAC, RSA, and Ed25519 keys.

evidence.claim: Binance offers OAuth for third-party applications
evidence.quote: The Binance OAuth allows users to share specific data with an 3rd application while keeping their accounts' API keys or login credentials

evidence.claim: The API surface spans many products (Spot, Futures, Options, Margin, Wallet, etc.), i.e. broad
evidence.quote: It covers the main programmatic interfaces available across Binance products, from market data access and account operations to advanced trading, streaming, and lower-latency integrations.

evidence.claim: Account verification (KYC) is a prerequisite for creating API keys (Binance.US docs)
evidence.quote: You will not be able to create an API if KYC is not completed.

notes: REST is primary, but WebSocket APIs/streams are also documented (market data, user data streams). Multiple base endpoints (api.binance.com, api-gcp, api1-api4) plus a market-data-only host data-api.binance.vision. Several third-party/community MCP servers exist (mcpservers.org/TermiX-official, nirholas/Binance-MCP, lobehub) but none are official; official docs do feature an 'Agent Native' section with llms.txt/llms-full.txt and an 'Agentic Wallet'/'Wallet Skills' area, suggesting official agent tooling, though no verbatim MCP mention in the supplied material. Binance.US is a separate regional API (docs.binance.us) with Exchange, Custodial, and Credit Line key types; custodial/credit-line keys require institutional agreements. Docs moved from binance-docs.github.io / binance-exchange GitHub org to developers.binance.com and github.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs. Old GitHub repo states: 'The Binance API documentation on Github has been moved to our official company repository'. A free Binance account suffices for keys, but KYC and 2FA are required; signed endpoints use HMAC/RSA/Ed25519 signatures with timestamp/recvWindow.
